R01.note: Honest and gives a correct five-step 500 sequence, but shows no code, gives no nullable fix for the guest-checkout case, and its opening is confusing.

errors: "every mistake in it becomes a 500" overstates, since a hand check can return 400
"what the 14 other handlers already read to know what a route accepts" is invented
"src/middleware/errors.ts catches one thing: ZodError" goes beyond the verified facts
R02.note: Strong TypeError-traversal sequence and labeled illustration, but it overstates the case and repeats the throw-type point in three sections.

R03.note: Tight and concrete, with the 400/500 sequence, the copied-response-shape cost of returning 400 by hand, and a nullable schema, though it never admits the earlier convention-only reason.

R04.note: Covers throw-Error, crash-TypeError and explicit-400 hand-rolled paths, the null drop, labeled code and unverified items, with a clear deciding rule.

errors: "nothing would make the next person do the same" is vague and unsupported
R05.note: Concise, with commented code, a nullable schema and the dropped-guest-event consequence, though the failure is a list rather than a full sequence.

errors: "miss that data.object.customer can now be null and cause a runtime crash": a typeof check does not crash on null
"guarantee that validation failures map to the correct HTTP status" ignores that strict zod also drops guest events
R06.note: Gets the 500/retry/page chain but uses verdicts, shows no code and mishandles the null case.

errors: "It also forces us to handle last week's change": zod forces nothing
"one malformed webhook ... turns into 3 days of retries and pages": one webhook alone does not exceed 5/min
R07.note: Terse and on point but inflates consequences and shows no code.

R08.note: Correct but thin, with "useful 400" and "enough failures" in place of named consequences or code.

errors: "the Express error handler every route's errors pass through" is slightly beyond the verified facts
R09.note: Admits the earlier label, gives a full sequence, a labeled illustration of the explicit-400 cost, and a both-sides null comparison with the nullable fix.

errors: invents the body of errors.ts as an illustration
implies zod handles a null customer, when a strict z.string() also rejects it
"If 5 guest checkouts arrive in a minute": the threshold is more than 5
ignores that a hand check can return 400
R10.note: Has a clear sequence but a misleading null story and an invented middleware body.

errors: "Keep the existing schema validation for this endpoint": the endpoint has no existing validation
its zod illustration uses z.string() and would also reject a null customer, which it leaves unaddressed
"catches throws from every route handler" goes beyond the verified facts
R11.note: Buried in glossary-style appositives, and its own zod schema repeats the null bug it criticises.

errors: "gets redelivered continuously" inflates retries that use backoff
"If you genuinely want zero dependency": zod is already a dependency
R12.note: Solid contract argument with a nullable schema, but ends in verdicts ("rebuilt the one thing zod does", "Use it") and some inflation.
